title: Dual-Dynamic In-Context Learning for Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Visual in-context learning (ICL) enables medical image segmentation models to adapt to new tasks using only a small set of annotated support images, without additional model fine-tuning. This makes visual ICL promising for clinical deployment, yet a fundamental limitation remains. Current ICL models lack the intrinsic ability to adaptively integrate supports based on their relevance to the query. By either aggregating supports uniformly or relying on external retrieval, these methods limit query-aware support integration within the model itself. We introduce Dual-DSA (Dual-Dynamic Support Alignment), a reliability-aware visual ICL framework that dynamically integrates supports at the patch and support-set levels. At the patch level, DynPatch-Align selectively attends to relevant support regions for each query location, enabling fine-grained contextual alignment. At the support set level, evidential fusion integrates support-conditioned predictions based on uncertainty and consistency, and provides an Aggregate Evidential Confidence Score for reliability assessment. Together, these mechanisms enable intrinsic, query-adaptive support integration across both levels. Extensive experiments on 11 medical imaging datasets across endoscopy, breast ultrasound, and thyroid ultrasound show that Dual-DSA achieves strong full-coverage performance, obtaining the best Dice score on 8 out of 11 datasets and consistently outperforming its attention-based ICL backbone. Furthermore, the derived confidence scores correlate with segmentation quality and enable confidence-based rejection to improve retained-case performance, providing a practical mechanism for quality control in clinical workflows.

title: Pseudoangiomatous Stromal Hyperplasia of the Breast: Clinical, Radiologic and Histopathologic Spectrum in a Retrospective Single-Centre Series.
abstract: Purpose Pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia (PASH) is a benign mesenchymal breast lesion with a broad spectrum of clinical and radiologic presentations. We aimed to evaluate the demographic, radiologic and histopathologic features of PASH-containing breast lesions. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included patients with histopathologically confirmed PASH identified between January 2019 and January 2026. Clinical records, mammography, ultrasonography, MRI findings and pathology reports were reviewed. Imaging findings were analysed descriptively together with demographic and histopathologic characteristics. Results Thirty-one female patients with a mean age of 34.1 ± 11.7 years (range, 11-51 years) were included. Most patients were premenopausal (29/31, 94%). PASH was most commonly identified as an incidental or associated stromal finding, particularly in fibroadenoma-spectrum lesions (18/31, 58%). On ultrasonography, the predominant appearance was an oval, parallel-oriented, hypoechoic lesion with circumscribed margins, although suspicious findings such as indistinct margins and non-parallel orientation were also observed. Mammographic findings ranged from negative examinations to mass-like densities and calcifications. MRI appearances were heterogeneous and included both mass and non-mass enhancement patterns. Two young patients demonstrated rapidly enlarging dominant diffuse/nodular PASH lesions with diffusion restriction on MRI, raising preoperative suspicion for angiosarcoma and ultimately requiring surgical management. Conclusion Breast PASH demonstrates substantial biologic and radiologic heterogeneity, ranging from incidental stromal findings within benign proliferative lesions to rapidly enlarging diffuse/nodular masses with aggressive imaging features mimicking angiosarcoma. Because imaging findings may reflect both the PASH component and associated breast pathology, radiologic-pathologic correlation is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate management.

title: Incremental value of pericarotid adipose tissue radiomics in predicting in-stent restenosis after carotid artery stenting.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the potential of pericarotid adipose tissue radiomics to improve the prediction of in-stent restenosis (ISR) after carotid artery stenting (CAS). Methods This retrospective study included 191 patients who underwent carotid CT angiography (CTA) and CAS within 1 week at two centers from September 2019 to December 2023. ISR was defined as ≥50% stenosis on follow-up Doppler ultrasound or CTA. Three predictive models were developed and defined as follows: Model A (Clinical), Model B (Clinical + Imaging), and Model C (Clinical + Imaging + Radiomics) using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. Results ISR occurred in 44 patients with a mean time interval of 11.3 months. Multivariate Cox regression analyses identified diabetes, fibrinogen, systolic blood pressure, calcified plaque volume, and pericarotid adipose tissue radiomics as independent predictors of ISR. The radiomics score, derived from 15 significant characteristics, outperformed conventional imaging markers. In the training set, Model C (AUC=0.881) significantly outperformed Model A (AUC=0.664) and Model B (AUC=0.840), with statistically significant differences (Model A vs Model C: P=0.001; Model B vs Model C: P=0.0246). This trend was consistent in the validation sets. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and actual ISR probabilities, and decision curve analysis indicated that Model C provided greater net benefits. Conclusion The radiomic characteristics of pericarotid adipose tissue provide incremental value in predicting ISR after CAS and serve as a valuable biomarker for restenosis risk assessment.

title: A comprehensive review on the current applications and future perspectives of radioembolization in endovascular neurosurgery.
abstract: In recent years, there has been advancement in the management of primary and secondary brain tumors within a multidisciplinary framework. However, substantial challenges persist in optimizing treatment strategies, enhancing survival rates, and improving patient prognosis and quality of life. These challenges stem from the complex interplay of biological processes that drive tumor pathogenesis and encompass factors such as tumor heterogeneity and patient variability together with surgical access and resectability in certain brain areas. Current therapeutic modalities - surgical resection, radiotherapy, and systemic pharmacotherapy - all have their own inherent limitations. However, promising alternative treatments are seen in emerging techniques such as endovascular radiosurgery, specifically ones that use intra-arterial delivery of radioactive Yttrium-90 ( 90 Y) microspheres. This approach is currently used in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treatment, which allows for the precise and targeted delivery of radiation to the tumor while minimizing systemic toxicity. Advances in imaging modalities such as MRI and single-photon emission computerized tomography (SPECT)/CT facilitate accurate dosimetry planning and ensure optimal therapeutic outcomes. This review provides the first comprehensive synthesis of the rationale, technical considerations, and translational potential of 90Y-based endovascular radiosurgery in neuro-oncology. While intra-arterial therapies and radiotherapy are established in other fields, their convergence for intracranial applications-particularly in bypassing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and achieving localized brachytherapy-remains in its early preclinical and clinical stages. We highlight specific central nervous system (CNS) use cases, preclinical findings, and procedural adaptations needed for this modality's advancement in brain tumor care.

title: A novel neurointerventional subarachnoid aqueductoplasty technique for the treatment of aqueductal stenosis: a cadaveric feasibility study.
abstract: Objective Aqueductal stenosis is a common cause of obstructive hydrocephalus, resulting in ventricular dilation and neurological deterioration. Standard treatments such as shunting, endoscopic third ventriculostomy, and traditional aqueductoplasty are effective but are associated with risks including parenchymal injury, infection, and long-term failure. As neurosurgery shifts toward minimally invasive techniques, there is a growing interest in approaches that avoid brain parenchyma transgression. This study introduces a novel neurointerventional method for treating aqueductal stenosis via the subarachnoid route through the foramen magnum and the fourth ventricle using standard endovascular tools. Methods Five formalin-fixed, silicone-injected, alcohol-preserved cadaveric heads were studied. Contrast was injected into the ventricular system. Catheters were introduced via simulated lumbar puncture or cisterna magna access and then advanced via the foramen of Magendie into the fourth ventricle and then through the aqueduct, utilizing Cone-beam CT, needle guidance software, and biplane fluoroscopy-guided navigation. A self-expanding stent was deployed in the aqueduct, and balloon aqueductoplasty was performed. Anatomical accuracy and technical success were confirmed via endoscopy through a transcallosal approach. Results Aqueductal access was successfully achieved in all specimens without brain parenchymal violation. Stent placement and balloon dilation were performed without complications and confirmed endoscopically. Conclusion This novel, image-guided, minimally invasive approach enables aqueductal catheterization via the subarachnoid route. It offers a brain-sparing alternative for treating aqueductal stenosis and may extend to future subarachnoid procedures such as third ventriculostomy or cyst fenestration. In vivo studies are warranted.

title: Visuospatial working memory in Huntington's disease: behavioural and structural brain correlates.
abstract: Background Visuospatial working memory (VSWM) deficits are among the earliest cognitive impairments evident in Huntington's disease (HD). They often precede motor symptoms and likely reflect early disruption of cortico-striatal circuits. Both the cognitive components and brain correlates are, however, poorly delineated. Objectives This study aims to characterise the progression of VSWM deficits across HD stages and identify their structural brain correlates. Methods In this prospective international study, 92 HD mutation carriers (HDmc) (21 premanifest and 71 manifest) and 39 healthy controls underwent cognitive and clinical assessments and structural MRI at baseline; 49 manifest HD and 36 controls completed a 1-year follow-up. VSWM was assessed using the object-location task (OLT), providing continuous measures of location error, object recognition and object-location binding. MRI analyses included caudate, putamen and hippocampal volumes and cortical thickness. Results We found increased location error and spatial imprecision under high memory load, without binding errors in premanifest HD with an area under the curve of 0.731. Across all HDmc, these location deficits correlated with striatal atrophy and cortical thinning in parietal and middle cingulate regions. Manifest HD individuals exhibited swap errors and hippocampal atrophy. Both location and swap errors worsened over time alongside progressive striatal and hippocampal volume loss. Principal component analysis confirmed a dissociation between spatial location-related deficits (striato-cortically mediated) and binding errors (hippocampally mediated), supporting a hierarchical model of VSWM decline. Conclusions HD-related VSWM impairment follows a staged, anatomically dissociable trajectory. The OLT offers sensitive, mechanistic markers of cognitive decline with potential utility for early detection and clinical trial stratification.

title: Facial Nerve Hemangioma in the Internal Auditory Canal: A Rare Localization and Therapeutic Challenge.
abstract: Objective Facial nerve hemangiomas (FNHs) are rare vascular tumors that often mimic other facial nerve disorders, making diagnosis and management challenging. This report highlights a case of FNH in the internal auditory canal (IAC) successfully treated via a translabyrinthine approach. Case presentation A 64-year-old female patient with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue presented with progressive left-sided peripheral facial paralysis (House-Brackmann Grade IV), associated with ipsilateral hearing loss and vertigo. MRI revealed a nodular lesion in the IAC with imaging features suggestive of a vascular origin. Due to symptom severity, surgical excision was performed using a translabyrinthine approach. Intraoperatively, a vascular lesion compressing but not infiltrating the facial nerve was excised, and histopathology confirmed FNH. Results The patient showed significant postoperative improvement, with facial nerve function improving to House-Brackmann Grade II at 6 months. Conclusion Early recognition and surgical intervention for symptomatic FNHs can prevent further neurological impairment. The translabyrinthine approach offers effective tumor removal while preserving facial nerve integrity.

A 64-year-old female patient with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue presented with progressive left-sided peripheral facial paralysis (House-Brackmann Grade IV), associated with ipsilateral hearing loss and vertigo. Intraoperatively, a vascular lesion compressing but not infiltrating the facial nerve was excised, and histopathology confirmed FNH.

The patient showed significant postoperative improvement, with facial nerve function improving to House-Brackmann Grade II at 6 months.

Conclusion

Early recognition and surgical intervention for symptomatic FNHs can prevent further neurological impairment. The translabyrinthine approach offers effective tumor removal while preserving facial nerve integrity.

title: Morphological computed tomography phenotypes in pulmonary sarcoidosis at diagnosis: splitting and lumping based on predictors of clinical progression.
abstract: Background Sarcoidosis may represent a broad umbrella term for various diseases that induce non-necrotising granulomas in affected organs. A recent multinational consensus proposed distinct computed tomography (CT) phenotypes for pulmonary sarcoidosis; however, the clinical implications remain unclear. What is the prevalence of individual phenotypes in a tertiary referral cohort, and are these phenotypes associated with disease progression? Materials and methods This retrospective study comprised 232 biopsy-proven pulmonary sarcoidosis patients treated between 2010 and 2020. Baseline CT scans were grouped into 1) non-fibrotic/fibrotic/unclear for fibrosis, and 2) normal/nodular/non-nodular. Disease progression was assessed over 36 months using predefined clinical, functional and therapeutic criteria. Results Most patients had non-fibrotic phenotypes (91.0%, n=211), while fibrotic (5.6%, n=13) and unclear (3.4%, n=8) patterns were less frequent. Inter-reader agreement was moderate for individual phenotypes (κ=0.55) and good for fibrotic versus non-fibrotic classification (κ=0.79). At 36 months, 69% of patients had progressed; all fibrotic cases progressed, compared with 67% of non-fibrotic. Nodular phenotypes progressed in a similar way to normal CT (64% versus 68%) and at a lower rate than non-nodular disease (88%). Fibrotic disease was associated with an increased risk of disease progression after adjustment for age, sex, body mass index and baseline lung function (hazard ratio 2.31, 95% CI 1.21-4.38; p=0.038). Conclusions CT-based phenotype assessment of sarcoidosis seems feasible but may require refinement. Fibrotic patterns predict progression, while nodular phenotypes carry a risk similar to normal CT. Further radiological splitting may not reflect distinct disease behaviour.

title: Deep learning radiomics based on preoperative multiparametric MRI in predicting breast cancer recurrence risk.
abstract: Background Breast cancer treatments are often tailored to recurrence risk to improve outcomes, but reliable risk stratification methods are lacking. Purpose To predict preoperative breast cancer recurrence risk through a tridimensional synergy model integrating breast MRI, radiomics, and deep learning. Study type Retrospective. Population 428 female patients were randomly divided into training (n = 299, 52.5 ± 12.2 years) and internal validation (n = 129, 53.2 ± 11.5 years) sets, with an external validation set of 196 patients (51.3 ± 11.2 years). Field strength/sequence Multiparametric 3T MRI included fat-suppressed T2-weighted (T2WI) spin-echo, axial diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) with one pre- and five post-contrast axial acquisitions. Assessment We compared recurrence-free survival (RFS) prediction among DLR, DLC, and DLRC models, selected the optimal DLRC to stratify patients by risk, assessed RFS differences, and validated predictions, confirming effective risk stratification. Statistical tests Continuous corrected chi-squared tests, one-way ANOVA, log-rank test. A two-tailed P< 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The DL model showed predictive capability for 3-year RFS, with AUCs of 0.75 (95% CI, 0.65-0.84) in the training set, 0.74 (95% CI, 0.56-0.92) in the internal validation set, and 0.65 (95% CI, 0.53-0.78) in the external validation set. The DLR model achieved improved AUCs of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.74-0.90), 0.83 (95% CI: 0.73-0.93), and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.55-0.80) for predicting 3-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) in the training, internal validation, and external validation sets, respectively. The DLC model outperformed the DL model alone. The DLRC model achieved the best performance in the training and internal validation sets. Its predictive ability remained discernible but was attenuated in the external validation set, with AUCs of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.91-0.99), 0.89 (95% CI: 0.79-0.99), and 0.79 (95% CI: 0.67-0.91) across the respective datasets. Data conclusion The DLRC model effectively predicted and stratified breast cancer recurrence risk by integrating deep learning, radiomics, and clinicopathological features. Evidence level 3. Technical efficacy Stage 5.

title: Ultrasound radiomics-based machine learning models for differentiating diabetic kidney disease from non-diabetic kidney disease in type 2 diabetes.
abstract: Background and objective Noninvasive differentiation of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) from non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains challenging, as conventional clinical markers and ultrasound imaging lack sufficient accuracy and reliability. This limitation often leads to unnecessary renal biopsies or delayed diagnosis. To address this gap, this study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model integrating renal ultrasound radiomic features and clinical predictors to distinguish DKD from NDKD in T2DM patients. Methods Patients with T2DM who underwent renal biopsy were retrospectively enrolled from three centers. Based on biopsy findings, patients were classified as DKD or NDKD, with overlapping lesions assigned to DKD. Renal ultrasound images were collected for ROI delineation and radiomic feature extraction. Clinical predictors were selected using logistic regression, correlation analysis, and LASSO. SVM, KNN, RF, and XGBoost models were developed using radiomic features alone or combined with clinical variables. Performance was evaluated by AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, and SHAP was used for model interpretation. Results Univariate analysis identified serum creatinine, eGFR, albumin and LDL‑C as significant variables, and eGFR was selected as the final clinical predictor after LASSO and multivariable logistic regression. The radiomics‑only model performed well in the training cohort but showed lower performance in the validation cohorts. The integrated model combining radiomic features with eGFR achieved AUCs of 0.991, 0.895 and 0.721 in the training, internal validation and external validation cohorts, respectively, with corresponding F1‑scores of 0.939, 0.815 and 0.714. DeLong's test further showed that XGBoost performed better than several comparator algorithms in the training and internal validation cohorts, whereas no significant differences were observed among models in the external validation cohort. Conclusion The XGBoost model integrating renal ultrasound radiomic features with eGFR showed favourable performance for differentiating DKD from NDKD in patients with T2DM. By using routinely available ultrasound images and a readily accessible clinical indicator, this model may serve as a non-invasive auxiliary tool for preliminary screening in primary-level hospitals or nephrology departments, providing supportive evidence for individualized assessment and renal biopsy decision-making.

title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: state of the art on diagnosis and current therapeutic approach.
abstract: Background Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common genetic cardiomyopathy and is characterized by unexplained myocardial hypertrophy. This condition exhibits marked clinical and prognostic heterogeneity. Advances in cardiovascular imaging techniques and genetic testing have significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy, phenotypic characterization, and prognostic assessment. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy can present with a broad spectrum of genetic substrates and clinical presentations, ranging from asymptomatic individuals to those with heart failure, arrhythmias, and even sudden cardiac death. The first-line method for diagnosis, risk stratification, and follow-up of these patients is echocardiography, but additional techniques, such as cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, provide complementary information, such as quantification of fibrosis, and more accurate measurements. Genetic testing contributes to etiological diagnosis and family screening. Treatment options include both pharmacological therapy (such as beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, and disopyramide), which is the first-line therapy, and septal reduction techniques (alcohol septal ablation, surgical myectomy), which should be reserved for selected patients. Recently, cardiac myosin inhibitors have emerged as a novel therapeutic option, demonstrating significant reductions in left ventricular outflow tract obstruction and improvement in symptoms. Conclusion Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy has evolved considerably with advances in imaging techniques, genetic evaluation, and targeted therapies. This review examines the primary diagnostic and management strategies, both established and emerging, for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

title: Human sporotrichosis in the Amazon: an emerging zoonosis and its clinical-epidemiological challenges.
abstract: The number of sporotrichosis cases in Brazil has been continuously increasing, primarily due to zoonotic transmission in urban areas. This study aimed to analyze the occurrence of human sporotrichosis in a reference center in the Amazon region. This case series study analyzed the medical records of patients diagnosed with sporotrichosis at a dermatology reference service in Northern Brazil. Most patients presented with the localized cutaneous form. Diagnosis was confirmed using clinical and epidemiological criteria, histopathology, and/or culture. Diagnostic suspicion, especially in endemic areas, and early treatment are essential to reduce morbidity, sequelae, and adverse outcomes.

title: Cerebral oxygen extraction fraction as an emerging imaging biomarker in mild cognitive impairment and dementia.
abstract: The progressive onset of dementia and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a major global health concern due to its profound impact on quality of life. The challenge of identifying MCI and dementia lies partly in the high cost and invasiveness of some biomarkers. In this context, the oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) has emerged as a promising imaging biomarker. This review summarizes current evidence on cerebral OEF as a neuroimaging biomarker in MCI and dementia, focusing on pathophysiology, imaging techniques, comparison with established biomarkers, clinical applications, and future directions. A literature search was conducted from July 1-31, 2025, using the United States National Library of Medicine (PubMed), Scopus, and Web of Science. Search terms included "oxygen extraction fraction" OR "cerebral oxygen metabolism" AND ("mild cognitive impairment" OR "MCI" OR dementia OR "Alzheimer's disease" OR "vascular dementia") AND (qBOLD OR TRUST MRI OR mcQQ MRI OR 15O PET). English-language studies from the past ten years reporting OEF in cognitive impairment were included; case reports and non-human studies were excluded. OEF demonstrates distinct alterations across the spectrum of cognitive impairment. In MCI, reduced OEF has been linked to impaired neurovascular coupling and mitochondrial dysfunction. In dementia, patterns diverge - typically reduced in Alzheimer's disease but heterogeneous in vascular conditions, often elevated under chronic hypoperfusion yet reduced when vascular pathology coexists with Alzheimer's disease. Non-invasive techniques such as mcQQ magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and TRUST MRI estimate OEF, while 15 O PET remains the gold standard. OEF shows promise as a neuroimaging biomarker for early detection, differential classification, and monitoring disease progression in cognitive impairment.

title: Changes in hip joint anatomical shape as a predictor of osteoarthritis.
abstract: Background Hip osteoarthritis (HOA) is one of the leading causes of musculoskeletal disability worldwide, yet its etiology remains incompletely understood. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving systemic factors and biomechanical alterations of the hip joint that trigger degenerative changes. Objectives The aim of this study was to identify the most informative radiographic views and the key acetabular and proximal femoral parameters for detecting structural abnormalities of the hip joint that may contribute to the development of HOA. Material and methods This observational case-control study included 156 patients older than 55 years who underwent total hip arthroplasty for HOA (osteoarthritis (OA) group) and 61 age-matched controls without clinical HOA, recruited from a single center between 2019 and 2022. Patient demographics, clinical history, and hip-specific functional scores were collected. Standardized anteroposterior (AP), frog-leg lateral (LL), and Dunn 45° radiographs were obtained, and multiple radiographic parameters were measured. Results Asymptomatic contralateral hips in patients with OA had significantly more cam-type deformities (higher alpha angles, lower head-neck offset ratios, and a higher prevalence of pistol-grip deformity) than those in the control group (p < 0.001). In contrast, pincer-type features were more common in the control group. Logistic regression analysis identified higher alpha angles, greater femoral neck diameter, and lower head-neck offset ratios as predictors of OA, whereas a larger femoral head diameter was identified as a protective factor (model area under the curve (AUC) = 0.90). Bone quality was superior in the control group, with longer femoral neck axis lengths and higher Singh indices (p < 0.001). Conclusions Radiographic markers of cam-type femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) are significantly more prevalent in patients with HOA and may serve as early indicators of disease risk. Dunn and LL views are optimal for detecting these abnormalities. A larger femoral head diameter, as measured on both AP and LL radiographic views, appears to be a protective factor against the development of HOA. Understanding these morphological differences may facilitate earlier diagnosis and support preventive strategies for HOA.

title: Beyond Static AI: Continual Learning Approaches for Long-Term Adaptation of Medical Imaging Systems
abstract: Deep learning now supports many tasks in medical imaging, but most systems assume a fixed data source and a single training event. Clinical practice is not static as new scanners arrive, protocols change, patient populations shift, and new diagnostic questions appear. A model that trains once and stays frozen tends to lose accuracy over time, while a model that retrains on new data alone tends to forget what it already knew, a failure known as catastrophic forgetting. Continual learning studies how a model can learn from a stream of data and tasks while it keeps prior knowledge. This survey reviews continual learning in medical imaging with a focus on recent progress. We report a reproducible review methodology, formalize the three learning scenarios, and organize the methods into five families: regularization, replay, dynamic architectures, foundation-model adaptation, and hybrids. We give particular attention to the shift toward frozen foundation models with lightweight adapters. We review applications across tasks and modalities, provide a critical analysis of study quality that distinguishes peer-reviewed work from preprints, and connect methods to the current regulatory framework for model updates. We close with open problems, aiming to provide researchers and clinical teams with a clear and up-to-date reference and to set out what remains to be shown before such systems can be updated safely in practice.

title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance in the Congenital Heart Disease Transition Clinic: Establishing the Adult Baseline for Lifelong Care—A Narrative Review
abstract: Advances in paediatric cardiology, surgery, intensive care and catheter interventions have enabled most children born with congenital heart disease (CHD) to reach adulthood. The transition from paediatric to adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) care remains a vulnerable period marked by risk of discontinuity, delayed recognition of residual lesions, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, aortopathy and other late complications. Cardiovascular imaging is therefore essential at this juncture. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) provides comprehensive, radiation-free assessment of anatomy, ventricular volumes and function, blood ﬂow, regurgitation, shunts and myocardial tissue characteristics. Its role in the transition clinic is not to replace echocardiography or to serve as a universal screening tool, but to resolve clinically important questions that echocardiography cannot answer reliably and to establish a reproducible quantitative baseline for lifelong adult follow-up. CMR is particularly valuable after repair of tetralogy of Fallot, in systemic right ventricles after atrial switch, in Fontan circulation, coarctation of the aorta, pulmonary artery abnormalities, anomalous venous connections, and other complex postoperative anatomies. Findings directly inﬂuence surveillance intervals, risk stratiﬁcation, exercise and pregnancy counselling, referral for catheterisation, and the timing of surgical or transcatheter reintervention. Limitations include examination duration, claustrophobia, arrhythmia-related degradation, device artefacts, contrast considerations, limited availability, and the need for congenital imaging expertise. A strategically timed CMR examination during transition bridges paediatric surgical history with adult care. By deﬁning an accurate adult baseline and detecting clinically silent abnormalities, CMR supports continuity, individualised surveillance, shared decision-making and lifelong management. Its use should remain lesion-speciﬁc, question-driven and integrated within a multimodality transition pathway.

CMR is particularly valuable after repair of tetralogy of Fallot, in systemic right ventricles after atrial switch, in Fontan circulation, coarctation of the aorta, pulmonary artery abnormalities, anomalous venous connections, and other complex postoperative anatomies. Findings directly inﬂuence surveillance intervals, risk stratiﬁcation, exercise and pregnancy counselling, referral for catheterisation, and the timing of surgical or transcatheter reintervention. Limitations include examination duration, claustrophobia, arrhythmia-related degradation, device artefacts, contrast considerations, limited availability, and the need for congenital imaging expertise. A strategically timed CMR examination during transition bridges paediatric surgical history with adult care. By deﬁning an accurate adult baseline and detecting clinically silent abnormalities, CMR supports continuity, individualised surveillance, shared decision-making and lifelong management. Its use should remain lesion-speciﬁc, question-driven and integrated within a multimodality transition pathway.

title: Non-Relapsing Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis in the Tolebrutinib Era: Global Evidence and a Proposed Clinical Implementation Pathway for the Gulf Cooperation Council
abstract: Background: In secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS), an apparently quiet relapse history can coexist with progressive loss of mobility, dexterity and independence. Tolebrutinib has made this discordance therapeutically consequential, but uncertainty about treatment applicability, serious hepatic toxicity and divergent regulatory judgments complicate translation into practice. In the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), early treatment access, cardiometabolic comorbidity and differences in care delivery make individualized assessment particularly important. Objectives: To examine the biological and clinical basis of potentially treatable progression without relapses; critically interpret the magnitude, functional relevance and limitations of therapeutic benefit; and develop a proposed GCC pathway connecting phenotype characterization, patient priorities, benefit–risk assessment and accountable longitudinal care. Methods: This structured critical evidence synthesis integrated six reproducible PubMed search blocks with targeted retrieval of clinical trials, human mechanistic studies, regulatory assessments, regional guidance and GCC clinical evidence through 7 September 2026. Purposive selection and narrative appraisal considered phenotype definitions, relapse and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) observation windows, endpoint construction, multiplicity, subgroup credibility, safety denominators and regional applicability. Absolute benefit was calculated from published fixed-time estimates. The pathway was developed by mapping evidentiary uncertainties to clinical assessment and implementation tasks; exhaustive screening and formal certainty grading were not undertaken. Results: Persistent inflammation, chronic lesion activity, accumulated neuroaxonal injury, impaired repair and diminishing neurological reserve provide an interacting explanation for progression after relapses subside. Clinically non-relapsing SPMS is distinct from longitudinally MRI-inactive disease, and progression independent of relapse activity is an operational event definition rather than proof of a specific mechanism. HERCULES randomized 1,131 participants and demonstrated a reduction in disability progression confirmed for six months using the Expanded Disability Status Scale with tolebrutinib versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.69; 95% confidence interval 0.55–0.88). Estimated 24-month progression risks were 21.9% and 30.2%, respectively: an author-calculated absolute difference of 8.3 percentage points, equivalent to approximately eight fewer progression events per 100 trial-like patients over two years. These population estimates do not establish individual benefit or efficacy specifically in longitudinally MRI-inactive SPMS. The upper-limb endpoint did not demonstrate benefit; subsequent favorable walking and disability-improvement estimates remained exploratory after hierarchical testing stopped. Severe liver injury and the negative PERSEUS trial in primary progressive MS reinforce the need for population-specific interpretation and careful benefit–risk assessment. US Food and Drug Administration refusal, European authorization accompanied by formal regulatory dissent, and United Arab Emirates (UAE) authorization illustrate consequential differences in judgments about benefit, uncertainty and acceptable harm. GCC vascular and metabolic comorbidity may contribute independently to functional deterioration and complicate disability attribution and treatment suitability; general-population prevalence cannot define the regional SPMS treatment population. Existing regional guidance and registries provide a foundation for implementation, although GCC-specific non-relapsing SPMS data remain limited. The proposed pathway integrates confirmation of sustained progression, dated relapse and MRI assessment, multidomain function, trial applicability, comorbidity and liver evaluation, current local authorization, shared decisions and named monitoring responsibility. Rehabilitation, symptom management and cardiometabolic care accompany every treatment decision. A focused registry extension supports prospective evaluation of classification reproducibility, implementation, effectiveness and safety. Conclusions: Absence of relapses should prompt precise characterization of ongoing progression while meaningful function remains available to preserve. Tolebrutinib establishes a therapeutic opportunity in a defined non-relapsing SPMS population, without resolving who benefits across all progressive phenotypes or functional domains. The contribution of this review is to connect that opportunity and its uncertainties to explicit, revisable clinical decisions. For the GCC, the proposed pathway requires prospective validation, with success judged by preservation of independence, reliable continuity of care and acceptable treatment burden and harm.

title: Metric Positional Encoding in Transformer-Based 3D Medical Image Segmentation Under Controlled Spacing Changes
abstract: Metric positional encoding supplies physical distances to Transformers, but its contribution to segmentation performance and spacing robustness remains uncertain. We evaluated whether metric coordinates improve performance, produce a more favorable response to resampling, and affect predictions through supplied spacing. A factorial UNETR comparison combined token-index or millimeter-based coordinates with additive Fourier encoding or 3D RoPE. KiTS23 evaluation used three-fold cross-validation on 391 patients; 117 eligible volumes were resampled to through-plane spacings of 3, 4, and 5 mm. Controls altered supplied spacing independently of image content. The RoPE comparison was repeated after retraining on AMOS22. In KiTS23, metric variants responded to supplied spacing but did not yield a more favorable Surface Dice change under resampling (contrast: −0.0029; 95% CI: −0.0104 to 0.0043). Among 38 eligible AMOS22 cases, metric RoPE retained higher absolute scores at every tested spacing, although its advantage narrowed from 0.0512 at native spacing to 0.0216 at 5 mm. Its baseline-relative response was less favorable (contrast: −0.0241; 95% CI: −0.0296 to −0.0186). These findings support evaluating absolute scores alongside changes from baseline and controls of spacing sensitivity. A less favorable change can coexist with higher absolute performance, conditional on the trained models and retrospective perturbations.

title: A case report of vulvar teratoma
abstract: Abstract Background Teratomas composed of tissues derived from all three germ layers are germ cell tumors originating from totipotent stem cells. While gonadal teratomas are common, extragonadal teratomas account for approximately 15% of all cases, with vulvar localization being exceptionally rare. To date, only a limited number of vulvar teratoma cases have been reported in the international literature. Case: A 19-year-old female presented with a vulvar mass first noted at birth that had progressively enlarged with age. Over the preceding year, the patient experienced intermittent inflammation and recurrent ulceration secondary to friction, accompanied by mild dysuria. Physical examination revealed a pedunculated mass measuring 5 × 4 cm situated between the clitoris and urethral meatus, together with a 2 × 2 cm urethral caruncle. Multimodal imaging including ultrasonography, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a mixed-echogenicity exophytic mass containing mesenteric and bowel-like structures with a prominent vascular pedicle extending toward the urethra and bladder trigone. The preoperative differential diagnosis included external parasitic twin (fetus in fetu) versus vulvar teratoma. The patient underwent complete surgical excision of the vulvar mass and the urethral caruncle under general anesthesia. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a mature teratoma. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed CK8/18 (+), CK20 (+), CDX-2 (+), Vimentin (+), and a Ki-67 proliferation index of less than 10%. The postoperative course was uneventful. At one-month follow-up, the wound had healed completely with restoration of normal vulvar anatomy and preserved physiological function. Conclusion Mature teratoma of the vulva is a rare extragonadal neoplasm that may be misdiagnosed on imaging as a parasitic twin owing to overlapping radiological features. Complete surgical excision remains the treatment of choice and is associated with favorable outcomes. Heightened clinical awareness and correlation of imaging findings with histopathological evaluation are essential to establish an accurate diagnosis and guide appropriate management in such rare cases.

title: Clinicopathological Determinants of Prognosis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Integrating Histopathology with an IHC-Based Molecular Subclassification
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a biologically heterogeneous malignancy that has undergone major therapeutic changes over the last two decades. Here, a real-world clinicopathological cohort integrating morphology, prognostic parameters, immunohistochemical surrogate markers for molecular stratification, and treatment outcome data is presented. Methods We performed a retrospective single-center study of 597 patients with histologically confirmed HCC (or occasional cases of combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) diagnosed at the Institute of Pathology, University of Regensburg, between 2000 and 2024. Clinical, pathological, laboratory, and follow-up data were merged with regional cancer registry data. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression. In a tissue microarray-based subcohort, immunohistochemistry for p53, Cyclin A2, Cyclin E1, β-catenin, and L-FABP1 was evaluated as a surrogate for a recently proposed molecular subclassification. Systemic treatment response and progression-free survival were assessed in patients with available follow-up data. Results The cohort comprised 486 men and 111 women, with a median age at diagnosis of 70 years in men and 67 years in women. Cirrhosis (49.7%), viral hepatitis (24.0%), diabetes mellitus (33.8%), arterial hypertension (45.2%), and steatosis hepatis (24.3%) were frequent background conditions. Median overall survival was 52 months. Survival declined with increasing grade and with incomplete resection. In multivariate Cox regression, older age, advanced T category, vascular invasion, positive resection margins, poor differentiation, macrotrabecular-massive (MTM) subtype, absence of tumor capsule, steatosis, and elevated alkaline phosphatase showed prognostic relevance, with age, T category, vascular invasion, resection status, MTM subtype, tumor capsule, and alkaline phosphatase emerging as particularly robust predictors. In the tissue microarray cohort, p53-high expression was independently associated with worse overall survival, whereas combined Cyclin A2/E1 high expression was significant in univariate analysis. L-FABP1 loss and nuclear β-catenin accumulation were not associated with outcome. Patients treated with atezolizumab/bevacizumab showed higher response rates than those treated with sorafenib. Conclusions This quarter-century single-center study highlights the multifactorial background, morphological diversity, and prognostic heterogeneity of HCC in routine clinical practice. Established clinicopathological variables remain the strongest determinants of survival, while p53 immunohistochemistry may provide additional prognostic information as an accessible molecular surrogate. The data further reflect the changing systemic treatment landscape from sorafenib to immunotherapy-based regimens in a real-world cohort.

title: Medical imaging in Bothrops lanceolatus envenomation: a retrospective series from Martinique
abstract: Abstract Background: Bothrops lanceolatus (Bl), a pit viper endemic to Martinique, is responsible for 40–50 envenomations annually. These are characterized by systemic thrombotic complications, that can lead to cerebral, myocardial, or pulmonary infarction. The introduction of the specific antivenom Bothrofav has substantially improved patient prognosis and management. Although severity grading remains primarily clinical, the specific role of medical imaging in this setting is underexplored. We aimed to delineate the contribution of imaging to the management of B. lanceolatus envenomation. Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study at the University Hospital of Martinique from January 2011 to August 2024. All patients with documented B. lanceolatus envenomation were included. We collected data in imaging use, clinical severity grade, and complications. Bivariate analyses were performed to examine associations between clinical status and imaging use. Results: A total of 389 patients were included (median age 48 years [IQR 35–59]; 128 [33%] women). Seventy-nine patients (20%) underwent at least one imaging examination, for a total of 127 studies. Imaging was infrequently used in mild envenomation (Grades 1–2) but significantly more frequent in severe cases (Grades 3–4, p < 0.01) and then complications were present, including compartment syndrome, shock, coma, infection, or the need for surgery. Eleven thrombotic events were confirmed in six pa three cerebral infarctions, three myocardial infarctions, two pulmonary embolisms, and three deep vein thromboses. Thoracic computed tomography (CT) and Doppler ultrasound were central to the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism and peripheral thrombosis, respectively. Conclusions: Although the management of snakebite envenomation remains primarily clinical, judicious use of medical imaging, specifically CT, MRI, and Doppler ultrasound, serves as a valuable adjunct. Imaging enhances severity grading and is essential for confirming thrombotic complications, thereby supporting the development of standardized, imaging-based management protocols for B. lanceolatus envenomation.

title: Comparison of One-Hole Split Endoscopy and Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy for Far-Lateral Lumbar Disc Herniation at L5/S1: A Short-Term Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes between One-hole Split Endoscopy (OSE) and Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy (UBE) for L5/S1 far-lateral lumbar disc herniation (FLLDH). Methods This retrospective study included 47 patients with L5-S1 FLLDH (July 2022-July 2024) divided into OSE and UBE groups. Surgical outcomes were documented. Radiographic parameters—including intervertebral foramen area (IVFA), height of the superior articular process (HSAP), lumbosacral lordotic angle (LLA), sagittal translation (ST), and disc height (DH)—were compared between groups. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Macnab criteria. Results Both groups exhibited significant improvement in VAS and ODI scores at all postoperative time points (P < 0.05), with no significant differences between groups. Excellent-to-good rates were 91.3% for OSE and 91.7% for UBE. One dural tear occurred in the OSE group. No significant intergroup differences were observed in any radiographic parameter. Postoperative ST and LLA remained stable (P > 0.05), whereas DH decreased, IVFA increased, and HSAP decreased (all P < 0.05). The UBE group demonstrated shorter operative time, while the OSE group had smaller incisions and less intraoperative blood loss. Conclusion Both UBE and OSE are effective minimally invasive approaches for treating L5-S1 FLLDH.

title: Low-Dose Esketamine Combined with Propofol for Sedation in Elderly Patients Undergoing Bidirectional Endoscopy: A single-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
abstract: Abstract Background Sedation for same-visit bidirectional gastrointestinal endoscopy in elderly patients remains a major clinical challenge. Propofol monotherapy carries a prominent risk of respiratory and circulatory depression, particularly in geriatric patients with limited physiological reserve. Esketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, exerts sympathomimetic effects that may offset propofol-induced hypotension and hypoxaemia. However, high-quality clinical evidence in this specific population is insufficient. This trial evaluated whether low-dose esketamine added to propofol reduces cardiopulmonary complications in elderly patients undergoing bidirectional endoscopy. Methods In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, 316 elective patients aged 60–80 years with ASA physical status I–III were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive either intravenous esketamine 0.15 mg/kg or normal saline placebo, followed by propofol 1 mg/kg for sedation induction. The dual primary outcomes were the incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxaemia. Prespecified secondary outcomes included procedural efficiency and quality indicators. Results The overall incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxaemia showed no significant intergroup differences. However, patients in the esketamine group maintained more stable intraoperative systolic blood pressure (SBP) and peripheral oxygen saturation (SPO₂) throughout the procedure. Esketamine also demonstrated superior procedural efficiency: shorter median induction time (120 s vs. 140 s; P < 0.001), 16.7% lower median propofol consumption (125 mg vs. 150 mg; P < 0.001), and 100% first-attempt gastroscope insertion success versus 94.9% with placebo (P = 0.007). Intraoperative bucking was halved (6.3% vs. 13.9%; P = 0.039). These gains were not offset by increased adverse events, including psychotomimetic effects, nausea and vomiting, dizziness, or cognitive impairment. Recovery times and patient satisfaction remained similarly high. Conclusions In conclusion, adjuvant low-dose esketamine combined with propofol did not reduce the incidence of intraoperative hypotension or hypoxemia in elderly patients undergoing same-visit bidirectional endoscopy. However, intraoperative SBP and SpO₂ were better preserved in patients receiving esketamine during the whole procedure. This regimen provided multiple clinical benefits including shortened induction time, higher first-pass gastroscopy insertion success rate, lower propofol dosage and reduced intraoperative bucking, without increasing overall adverse event risks. Trial registration Trial registration: This trial was prospectively registered on 26 March 2025 in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (registration number ChiCTR2500099643; https://www.chictr.org.cn/).

title: Lichen Sclerosus, Breast Cancer, and the Impact of Hormonal Therapy: A Large-Scale Propensity-Matched Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate the bidirectional association between lichen sclerosus and breast cancer, and to assess whether hormonal breast cancer therapies influence the subsequent risk of developing lichen sclerosus. Methods: This retrospective cohort study utilized a global electronic health record network containing over 204 million patients. Female patients with lichen sclerosus were compared to matched controls with postmenopausal atrophic vaginitis. Reciprocally, breast cancer patients were compared to matched controls who underwent mammography without a cancer diagnosis. Cohorts were propensity-score matched for age, race, ethnicity, body mass index, and smoking status. Results: Among 77,386 patients with lichen sclerosus and 77,163 controls, lichen sclerosus was associated with a lower incidence of subsequent breast cancer (2.22% vs. 2.55%; RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.93, p<0.001). Conversely, in 563,498 breast cancer patients without hormonal therapy versus 563,676 controls, breast cancer was associated with a higher incidence of subsequent lichen sclerosus (0.18% vs. 0.10%; RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.67-2.04, p<0.001). Hormonal therapy exposure in breast cancer patients showed a minimal risk increase for lichen sclerosus (RR 1.07, p=0.031), with no significant association found for tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors specifically. Conclusion: Lichen sclerosus is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer, whereas breast cancer is associated with a higher subsequent incidence of lichen sclerosus. Because this increased risk persists in patients who did not receive hormonal therapy, mechanisms beyond estrogen deprivation likely drive the development of lichen sclerosus in breast cancer patients.

title: Preserved consciousness as a diagnostic pitfall: a case report of tramadol-induced serotonin syndrome with isolated neuromuscular symptoms in an adolescent after general anesthesia
abstract: Abstract Background Serotonin syndrome (SS) typically presents with altered mental status, autonomic dysfunction, and neuromuscular abnormalities. We report an atypical case of perioperative tramadol-induced SS in an adolescent characterized by isolated neuromuscular symptoms with completely preserved consciousness and stable autonomic function, challenging the established paradigm that altered mental status and hyperthermia are obligatory for diagnosis. Case presentation: A 13-year-old girl (54 kg,body mass index 23.4 kg/m²) underwent arthroscopic meniscus repair under general anesthesia with fentanyl. One hour postoperatively, tramadol 50 mg (0.93 mg/kg) was administered intravenously. Ten minutes later, she developed right-hand tremor progressing to bilateral paroxysmal convulsions. Crucially, she remained fully conscious, coherent, and oriented throughout, accurately recalling the convulsive process. Continuous monitoring revealed stable hemodynamics without hyperthermia (maximal temperature 37.2°C). Emergent non-contrast head computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed no structural abnormalities. Blood gas analysis showed metabolic acidosis (lactate 6.0 mmol/L) and electrolyte disturbances. After midazolam sedation and electrolyte correction, symptoms recurred. Multidisciplinary consultation and Hunter criteria application confirmed SS. Treatment included tramadol discontinuation, midazolam infusion, and supportive care, leading to symptom resolution within 3 days. Conclusions This case represents a rare abortive form of SS characterized by isolated neuromuscular manifestations without autonomic or mental status changes. Anesthesiologists should not exclude SS based on intact mental status or normothermia; Hunter criteria should be applied immediately when abnormal neuromuscular symptoms occur postoperatively in patients with recent serotonergic drug exposure. The proposed cortico-spinal dissociation mechanism may explain this consciousness-sparing phenotype, though it requires further validation.

title: Comparing Quantitative CT Patterns in Silicosis and Welder’s Pneumoconiosis: Significant Correlations with Lung Function and Identification of a Bimodal Histogram Pattern
abstract: Abstract Background: Given its progressive nature and compensation requirements, early diagnosis and objective monitoring of pneumoconiosis are essential. This study compared quantitative computed tomography (QCT) patterns in silicosis and welder’s pneumoconiosis (WP) and assessed their correlation with lung function. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 60 patients with pneumoconiosis, comprising 30 with silicosis and 30 with WP. Two radiologists, blinded to exposure data, performed QCT analysis. QCT parameters were compared between the study groups. Spearman correlation analyses were conducted between pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and QCT parameters, and between PFTs and the International Labour Organisation (ILO) classification categories. Results: In the silicosis group, a second peak, typically clustered within the range of -200 to +200 Hounsfield units (HU), was observed. This “Secondary peak” (bimodal histogram) was significantly associated with silica exposure, higher perfusion categories, and larger opacity sizes (p = 0.001, 0.007, and <0.001, respectively). Mean lung density showed a moderate negative correlation with both forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1, rho = −0.46) and forced vital capacity (FVC, rho = −0.53), whereas no significant association was found between ILO classification and PFTs. Conclusion: We defined the secondary peak in histogram analysis, linking it to increased opacity size, profusion, and silica exposure. QCT, which better reflects lung function than the ILO classification, may represent a promising option for monitoring pneumoconiosis.

title: Clinical Observation of CD7-Directed CAR-T cell Therapy in Relapsed/Refractory Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukaemia
abstract: Abstract Mixed phenotype acute leukaemia (MPAL) currently lacks a specific target for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and effective treatment options for patients with relapsed/refractory disease remain limited. CD7-directed CAR-T cell therapy has achieved high complete remission rates with a favourable safety profile in patients with relapsed/refractory T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (R/R T-ALL). Given that CD7 is expressed on leukaemic blasts in a subset of patients with MPAL, we therefore used humanised CD7-directed CAR-T (hCD7 CAR-T) cells as salvage therapy in selected patients with relapsed/refractory MPAL (R/R MPAL) and evaluated the safety and efficacy of this approach. Between April 2024 to December 2025, seven patients with R/R MPAL who received hCD7 CAR-T therapy were retrospectively analysed. All patients had CD7 expression > 80% on leukaemic cells by flow cytometry. CAR-T cells were generated through transduction with a second-generation CAR lentiviral vector encoding CD3ζ-4-1BB. Before CAR-T infusion, patients received a lymphodepletion regimen based on fludarabine and/or cyclophosphamide. CAR-T cells were cultured for 5–8 days and then infused into patients. Treatment efficacy was assessed on day 30 after infusion. Minimal residual disease (MRD) was evaluated using FCM and quantitative PCR methods. Extramedullary lesions were assessed by PET/CT, CT, or ultrasonography. Patients were followed regularly until 30 April 2026. The median age was 33 years (range 18–70). Five patients had bone marrow haematological relapse (including 3 patients with extramedullary lesions), 2 patients had bone marrow MRD-positive disease, and 1 patient had relapsed after transplantation. The median infused CAR-T cell dose was 5.0 × 10⁵/kg (range 1.0–9.0 × 10⁵/kg). The major treatment-related adverse event was cytokine release syndrome (CRS), and all cases were Grade 1. Five patients received supportive treatment, 1 patient received supportive treatment and corticosteroids, and 1 patient received supportive treatment, corticosteroids, siltuximab, and etoposide. Symptoms improved in all patients, and no treatment-related mortality occurred. At day 30 after CAR-T infusion, 6 patients achieved complete remission (CR), including 1 patient with MRD-positive CR, resulting in a complete remission rate of 85.7%. One patient showed no response. The median follow-up duration was 8.3 months (range 4.7–24.4). All patients underwent bridging allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) 5–8 weeks after CAR-T therapy. Five patients achieved continuous complete remission (CCR), with remission durations of 24.4, 12.5, 6.0, 5.2, and 4.7 months, respectively. One patient relapsed at 7 months post-transplant, and one non-responder patient experienced bone marrow haematological relapse and multiple extramedullary relapses at 6.9 months post-transplant and died of disease progression. In conclusion, hCD7 CAR-T therapy demonstrated a high CR rate of 85.7% and a favourable safety profile in patients with CD7-positive R/R MPAL. Durable remissions were achievable with bridging allo-HSCT, though patients failing to respond had a poor prognosis.

title: Ultra-Early Postmortem 3-T MRI of the Human Brain: A Two-Case Feasibility Study of Structural, Diffusion, and Vascular Imaging in Unfixed Cadavers
abstract: Abstract Background Cadaveric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) permits high-resolution, motion-free characterization of neuroanatomy, but postmortem interval, tissue temperature, autolysis, and chemical fixation can alter relaxation and diffusion properties. Imaging rapidly after death and before fixation may reduce exposure to these time-dependent changes, but the feasibility of combining sub-millimeter structural imaging, advanced diffusion imaging, and vascular imaging on a clinical 3T platform remains incompletely characterized. We therefore assessed the technical feasibility of these acquisitions in a two-cadaver exploratory series. Methods This exploratory two-case feasibility series included two adult cadavers studied at a short postmortem interval on a clinical 3T MRI system. Acquisitions included T1-weighted MPRAGE, T2-weighted SPACE, susceptibility-weighted imaging, diffusion spectrum imaging, multi-shell diffusion-weighted imaging, and time-of-flight angiography. In one specimen, postmortem vascular perfusion with manganese chloride was followed by additional angiographic imaging. Structural, diffusion, and vascular datasets underwent modality-specific preprocessing, reconstruction, and visual quality review. Feasibility was evaluated descriptively; no inferential statistical tests or population-level effect estimates were performed. Results Sub-millimeter structural MRI and advanced diffusion imaging were acquired and reconstructed in both specimens. Whole-brain deterministic tractography was generated in both cases. In specimen 1, a focal structural abnormality compatible with a chronic lacunar infarct was accompanied by a visually reduced streamline representation in the corresponding region. In the perfused specimen, post-perfusion angiographic imaging enabled visualization and 3D reconstruction of major proximal intracranial vessels and showed reduced distal vascular opacification in the right middle cerebral artery territory. These focal structural, diffusion, and vascular observations were exploratory rather than prespecified diagnostic endpoints. Conclusions In this two-specimen series, ultra-early unfixed cadaveric MRI on a standard clinical 3T platform yielded interpretable high-resolution structural and diffusion datasets, with a technically usable vascular reconstruction in the perfused case. These findings support workflow feasibility but do not establish diagnostic accuracy, preservation of in vivo tissue properties, reproducibility, or generalizability.

title: The Carcinoembryonic Antigen-to-Skeletal Muscle Index Ratio as a Novel Prognostic Marker in Colorectal Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and sarcopenia, defined as a low skeletal muscle index (SMI), are established prognostic factors in colorectal cancer (CRC). We evaluated the prognostic value of the preoperative CEA-to-SMI ratio (CSR), an index integrating tumor burden and host physiological reserve. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 1,033 patients who underwent curative surgery for CRC. SMI (cm²/m²) was measured on preoperative computed tomography at the third lumbar vertebra, and patients were stratified into CSR quartiles (Q1–Q4). The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Independent prognostic factors were identified by multivariable Cox regression, and discrimination was compared with that of CEA and SMI alone using Harrell's concordance index (C-index). Results Five-year OS decreased stepwise as the CSR increased: 93.4% (Q1), 86.8% (Q2), 83.2% (Q3) and 76.6% (Q4) ( P < 0.001). On multivariable analysis the CSR remained an independent prognostic factor, with Q4 carrying a higher risk of death than Q1 (hazard ratio 2.650, 95% confidence interval 1.610–4.360; P < 0.001). The C-index of the CSR (0.625) was higher than that of CEA alone (0.574, P < 0.001) or SMI alone (0.574, P = 0.039). Adding the CSR to a base clinical model improved the C-index from 0.714 to 0.728 ( P = 0.041). Conclusion The preoperative CSR is a potentially useful independent prognostic indicator in CRC, providing additive risk stratification beyond CEA or SMI alone and enabling identification of high-risk patients in clinical practice.

title: Synthesis, Radiolabeling, and Biological Evaluation of an RGD-Conjugated 99ᵐTc Dendrimer for Breast Cancer SPECT Imaging
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Early and accurate molecular imaging is essential for improving diagnosis and patient outcomes. Nanotechnology-based imaging probes offer promising opportunities to overcome limitations associated with tumour heterogeneity. Materials and Methods Third-generation polyethylene glycol (PEG)–citrate dendrimers were synthesised and functionalised with arginylglycylaspartic acid (RGD) peptides targeting αvβ3 integrins. The nanoconjugates were radiolabeled with technetium-99m ( 99 mTc) and characterised using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering (DLS), and electron microscopy. In vitro cytotoxicity was assessed using the XTT assay. In vivo imaging and biodistribution studies were conducted in tumour-bearing nude mice using single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT). Results The synthesised dendrimers demonstrated favourable physicochemical properties and high radiochemical purity. In vitro assays confirmed good biocompatibility, with no significant cytotoxicity observed at concentrations up to 8 mg/mL. SPECT imaging revealed rapid and specific tumour accumulation within the first hour post-injection, with maximal uptake observed at approximately 90 minutes. Biodistribution studies indicated predominant renal clearance and minimal nonspecific uptake in non-target organs. The radiolabeled nanoconjugates remained stable in human serum for up to 24 hours. Conclusion RGD-functionalized, 99 mTc-labeled PEG–citrate dendrimers exhibit strong potential as targeted SPECT imaging agents for breast cancer. Their favourable targeting specificity, imaging contrast, and pharmacokinetic profile support further development for molecular imaging and theranostic applications.

title: Treatment outcomes of a combination with intensity-modulated radiotherapy and three fractions of computed tomography-guided brachytherapy for uterine cervical cancer: A single-institution analysis in Japan
abstract: Abstract Background To evaluate the midterm treatment outcomes, efficacy, and safety of a radiotherapy (RT) regimen combining intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and a reduced three-fraction schedule of computed tomography (CT)-guided brachytherapy (BT) for uterine cervical cancer (UCC). Methods This retrospective study evaluated patients with UCC (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stages IB–IVB) treated at our institution between May 2017 and December 2023. The patients received whole-pelvic IMRT (45–50.4 Gy) with an adjustable boost for enlarged lymph nodes followed by 3 fractions of CT-guided high-dose-rate BT. The primary endpoint was the local control (LC) rate; the secondary endpoints were disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and late toxicities. Results A total of 92 patients were included, and 77 patients received platinum-based concurrent chemotherapy. The median follow-up period was 43.5 months. The median total high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) D90 dose was 77.1 Gy. The 3-year LC, DFS, and OS rates were 94.5%, 66.5%, and 86.2%, respectively. T stage was an independent prognostic factor for both LC and DFS, whereas T stage and HR-CTV at initial BT were independent prognostic factors for OS. Grade ≥ 3 late toxicities were observed in 4 patients (4.3%). Conclusions The combination of IMRT and a reduced 3-fraction CT-guided BT achieves good LC with acceptable toxicity in patients with stage IB–IVB UCC. This regimen offers a reasonable and practical approach to minimize patients’ physical and psychological burden, although a more intense treatment should be considered for patients with advanced-stage disease.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Quantum and Quantum-Inspired Image Segmentation in the Context of Modern Segmentation Methods
abstract: Abstract Image segmentation remains one of the most extensively studied problems in computer vision, with applications ranging from medical image analysis and autonomous driving to remote sensing and industrial inspection. While deep learning approaches currently dominate the field, interest in quantum computing has motivated the development of quantum and quantum-inspired segmentation techniques that explore alternative strategies for image representation, optimization, and learning. This survey provides a comprehensive review of quantum and quantum-inspired image segmentation methods within the broader context of modern segmentation research. To establish this context, we first examine the evolution of image segmentation methodologies, covering classical image processing techniques, machine learning approaches, and contemporary deep learning architectures.We then organize the existing quantum image segmentation literature into four categories: quantum-inspired, tensor network-based, hybrid quantum-classical, and fully quantum methods. Across these categories, we analyze computational principles, image encoding and representation strategies, application domains, and datasets. We further compare quantum and quantum-inspired approaches with established segmentation paradigms in terms of supervision, scalability, and hardware requirements. Our analysis indicates that quantum-inspired methods currently represent the most developed direction, while hybrid approaches are emerging and fully quantum methods remain constrained by quantum hardware, data encoding costs, and scalability challenges. By connecting quantum image segmentation with the broader evolution of segmentation research, this survey provides a unified perspective on the field. It identifies current trends, open challenges, and promising future directions for researchers exploring the emerging role of quantum computing in image segmentation.

To establish this context, we first examine the evolution of image segmentation methodologies, covering classical image processing techniques, machine learning approaches, and contemporary deep learning architectures.We then organize the existing quantum image segmentation literature into four categories: quantum-inspired, tensor network-based, hybrid quantum-classical, and fully quantum methods. Across these categories, we analyze computational principles, image encoding and representation strategies, application domains, and datasets. We further compare quantum and quantum-inspired approaches with established segmentation paradigms in terms of supervision, scalability, and hardware requirements. Our analysis indicates that quantum-inspired methods currently represent the most developed direction, while hybrid approaches are emerging and fully quantum methods remain constrained by quantum hardware, data encoding costs, and scalability challenges. By connecting quantum image segmentation with the broader evolution of segmentation research, this survey provides a unified perspective on the field. It identifies current trends, open challenges, and promising future directions for researchers exploring the emerging role of quantum computing in image segmentation.

title: Computerized Tomography Based Evaluation of Morphometric and Angular Parameters of the Adult Femur among Kenyans
abstract: Abstract Background The femur and the pelvis are large weight bearing bones in the human body. The femur, the bone of the thigh region, is the longest and strongest bone. Anatomically, the femur is divided into proximal, mid and distal segments. The evaluation of the structural morphology of body structures using Computer Tomography (CT) scan enables 3-dimensional evaluation; study of both the external and internal anatomy of bones without necessitating their destruction and the evaluation of the relationship of bone structures with vital structures such as nerves and vessels. This radiological evaluation of the Femur would inform placement of intramedullary devices and safe surgical approaches for both open and minimally invasive surgeries. Objective To describe the radiological topography of the adult femur in Kenya. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital and St. Luke’s Orthopaedic and Trauma Hospital. Lower limb CT scan images from 120 participants of either sex aged at least 18 years were analysed. Three-dimensional reconstruction was performed using MATLAB 9.7, and measurements were analysed using STATA/MP 13.0. Morphometric and angular parameters were summarized using mean and corresponding standard deviation. Results Morphometric parameters of the femur revealed a mean anteroposterior (AP) width at the isthmus of 13.987 ± 2.265 mm and mediolateral (ML) width at the isthmus of 10.943 ± 2.598 mm. Angular parameters included a mean proximal diaphysis angle (PDA) of 8.871 ± 2.282° and distal diaphyseal angle of 9.358° (± 2.331). Conclusion The study provides key anatomical parameters of the femur and pelvis, which can inform the design of implants tailored for the local population. These findings also support improved surgical planning and fracture stabilization techniques.

title: Integrating NHANES and a Real-World Clinical Cohort to Evaluate the Consistent Dose-Response Association Between MHR and Osteoarthritis
abstract: Abstract Background Emerging evidence highlights the key role of chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic disorders in osteoarthritis (OA) pathogenesis. The monocyte-to-HDL-C ratio (MHR) serves as a promising integrated biomarker linking pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory status, yet its relationship with OA remains unclear. This study investigated the dose-response association between MHR and OA risk using the NHANES cohort and an independent clinical validation cohort with radiographic Kellgren-Lawrence grading. We further explored the potential mediating effect of body mass index (BMI) in this association. Methods This study adopted a two-stage discovery-validation design to investigate the association between MHR and OA. For the discovery phase, weighted data from 70,190 participants enrolled in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) during 2005–2018 were subjected to comprehensive statistical analysis. For the subsequent external validation phase, an independent clinical cohort comprising 500 hospital-based patients was utilized, with OA diagnosis in this cohort strictly established according to the K-L grading system. To assess the robustness of the association and its dose-response relationship, multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and subgroup analyses were applied across both study phases. Additionally, mediation analysis was conducted to quantify the proportion of the MHR-OA association mediated by body mass index (BMI). The clinical predictive value of MHR for OA was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), while two-piecewise linear regression analysis was employed to identify the optimal risk threshold of MHR for OA. Results In the NHANES cohort, MHR levels were significantly higher in patients with OA compared to non-OA participants ( P < 0.001). After full adjustment, MHR remained significantly associated with an increased risk of OA ( OR = 1.15, 95% CI : 1.04–1.26, P < 0.050). RCS regression revealed a consistent non-linear positive dose-response relationship, which was robust across most subgroups. Mediation analysis further indicated that BMI mediated 22.18% of the association between MHR and OA in the discovery cohort. These findings were successfully replicated in the independent clinical validation cohort, where BMI accounted for 23.01% of the total effect ( P < 0.001). Furthermore, MHR remained a strong independent predictor of OA ( OR = 2.64, 95% CI : 2.13–3.27, P < 0.001). In the clinical setting, MHR exhibited favorable diagnostic utility with an AUC of 0.839 (95% CI : 0.797–0.881, P < 0.001). Additionally, threshold effect analysis identified an inflection point at MHR = 4.12, beyond which the risk of OA increased significantly. Conclusion Our findings established MHR as a robust, independent, and cost-effective biomarker for OA risk, driven significantly by BMI-related metabolic pathways. The consistent results across population-based and clinical-based cohorts supported the use of MHR as a compelling tool for risk stratification and clinical screening.

title: The updated 2022 Fédération Cynologique Internationale method may lead to changes in hip dysplasia grading in some dogs.
abstract: Objective To compare Norberg angle (NA) measurements and hip dysplasia (HD) grades obtained from the same radiographs using the Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) 2022 (FCI22) and FCI 2006 methods (FCI06). Methods This retrospective observational study included radiographs submitted for canine HD screening from March 17, 2023, through September 27, 2024. Radiographs meeting FCI quality standards were evaluated under both methods, with NA measurements and HD grades recorded accordingly. Grade changes were classified as upgraded, downgraded, or unchanged. Results Radiographs from 1,020 Australian Shepherds and 298 Boxers were reviewed. The mean Norberg angle measured according to the 2022 method (NA22) was 0.7° lower than that measured according to the 2006 method (NA06). Overall, 1,801 of 2,636 hips (68.3%) retained the same HD grade with the FCI22. In Australian Shepherds, 350 of 2,040 hips (17.2%) were upgraded, and 257 of 2,040 hips (12.6%) were downgraded. In Boxers, 53 of 596 hips (8.9%) were upgraded, and 175 of 596 hips (29.4%) were downgraded. Reclassification occurred primarily among hips initially graded D in 2006 (D06), with 286 of 347 hips (82.4%) reclassified. Conclusions Differences between NA22 and NA06 had limited impact on HD grading except for hips with near-threshold NA values. The FCI22 kept most HD grades unchanged. Across both breeds, upgrades occurred primarily among grade D hips. Breed differences in grade changes may reflect interbreed anatomical differences. Clinical relevance The FCI22 method is unlikely to substantially alter HD grades in these 2 breeds. Borderline hips and breed-specific grading patterns may affect individual screening outcomes.
